description: Thirty manually authored and labeled synthetic selection examples. These are fictional rubric tests, not claims about the named institutions. Ten cases per source group; positive and difficult negative cases are intentional. Real-world precision must also be reviewed on live findings.

examples.title: Alpine ice reference archive
examples.text: The Alpine Ice Reference Archive preserves a continuous 800,000-year climate record. It is the reference dataset used by 34 international climate modeling teams to validate reconstructions, and the university provides calibrated samples and measurement services to outside research partners. The archive opened in 2004 and remains operational.
examples.label_reason: Distinctive established infrastructure with documented international use, despite its age.

examples.title: Institute picnic
examples.text: The institute held its annual picnic on Friday. More than 80 colleagues attended and enjoyed a talk about recent research. The director thanked the organizing team and announced that next year's picnic would take place in the same park. Photographs of the event are available to staff.
examples.label_reason: Routine social event with no substantive research outcome.

examples.title: Orbital clock demonstration
examples.text: The Bern Orbital Clock experiment delivered the first continuous optical time-transfer link on the mission, maintaining synchronization within 20 picoseconds during the six-month orbital trial. The validated hardware was adopted for the mission's navigation system. The experiment was completed in 2012.
examples.label_reason: Specific demonstrated technical achievement and adopted application; historical status matters.

examples.title: Paper in a prestigious journal
examples.text: A team published a short commentary in the prestigious International Science Review. The commentary discusses why collaboration is useful and summarizes existing literature. The institute congratulates the authors on this outstanding publication and their excellent contribution to scientific dialogue.
examples.label_reason: Prestigious venue and promotional praise do not establish a significant result.

examples.title: National biodiversity observatory
examples.text: The National Biodiversity Observatory coordinates a CHF 40 million national program involving 18 institutions. Its standardized long-term measurements now support the country's biodiversity reporting framework. University of Bern leads the scientific program and operates the openly accessible measurement platform.
examples.label_reason: Strategic national program, substantial scale and concrete application.

examples.title: Research assistant vacancy
examples.text: Applications are invited for a research assistant position in the nationally funded biodiversity program. The successful candidate will help process samples, organize meetings and maintain the laboratory inventory. Employment is for one year. Applications should include a curriculum vitae and two references.
examples.label_reason: Vacancy, even though it mentions a potentially important program.

examples.title: Catalyst transfer agreement
examples.text: The Bern Circular Catalyst process converts mixed polymer waste into reusable monomers at a demonstrated recovery rate of 94 percent in a continuous pilot line. A signed license agreement transfers the patented process to an industrial operator for plant integration. The result and the signed agreement are reported together.
examples.label_reason: Measured process capability and documented technology transfer.

examples.title: Weekly microscopy seminar
examples.text: A visiting scientist will introduce the basics of fluorescence microscopy during the weekly seminar. The event is open to students and staff. No new instrument, research result or service is being announced. Participants can bring a packed lunch and ask questions after the lecture.
examples.label_reason: Teaching event without a new research outcome.

examples.title: Incremental local survey
examples.text: A sociology group interviewed twelve students about cafeteria opening hours. The descriptive results confirm that most participants prefer a later closing time, in line with previous local surveys. The authors recommend a larger survey before drawing broader conclusions. A short report has been placed on the group website.
examples.label_reason: Substantive but secondary finding with limited scope.

examples.title: International historical research award
examples.text: The Bern Manuscript Reconstruction project received the international Grand Prize for Historical Scholarship for reconstructing and publishing a previously inaccessible archive of 70,000 documents. Its openly released critical edition has been adopted by 26 university history departments for primary-source research. The project concluded in 1998.
examples.label_reason: Major recognition and documented scholarly contribution, without a date cutoff.

examples.title: Adaptive hearing implant platform
examples.text: The Adaptive Hearing Implant platform restores closed-loop stimulation using patient-specific feedback. In a multicenter controlled study with 240 participants it improved speech recognition by 18 percentage points against the reference device. The platform has been licensed to a manufacturer. ARTORG led the engineering development.
examples.label_reason: Specific clinical evidence and transfer; not merely a promising prototype.

examples.title: Our world-leading laboratory
examples.text: Our laboratory is world-leading, innovative and excellent. We conduct cutting-edge research and work with outstanding partners to shape tomorrow's healthcare. Our talented staff are passionate about breakthroughs and strive to make a difference. Visit our news page to learn more about our exciting journey.
examples.label_reason: Marketing adjectives without concrete outcomes or distinctive capability.

examples.title: Perfused organ testing facility
examples.text: The Perfused Organ Testing Facility combines vascularized human tissue chips with continuous mechanical and biochemical monitoring. It provides validated drug-response assays unavailable in conventional static cell cultures, and accepts external research projects through a published access procedure. ARTORG operates the facility.
examples.label_reason: Distinctive infrastructure with a specified application and explicit access.

examples.title: Printer maintenance update
examples.text: The laboratory's standard desktop printer will be unavailable on Tuesday for routine maintenance. A replacement toner cartridge has been ordered and staff can use the printer on the second floor. The service desk will announce when normal printing resumes. No research equipment is affected.
examples.label_reason: Routine administrative notice.

examples.title: National surgical robotics flagship
examples.text: The National Surgical Robotics Flagship is a CHF 25 million program led by ARTORG and six clinical centers. It integrates robotic navigation and intraoperative sensing in a shared evaluation platform. The funded five-year program has launched and its published milestones include a coordinated multicenter validation study.
examples.label_reason: Explicitly funded strategic program with defined work and partners; outcomes must not be invented.

examples.title: Promising sensor pilot
examples.text: An exploratory study tested a new wearable signal in five healthy volunteers. Correlation with the reference was modest and the study had no control group. The authors state that no clinical utility has yet been demonstrated and that extensive validation is needed. They describe the concept as promising for future investigations.
examples.label_reason: Small exploratory study without demonstrated significance; promise is insufficient.

examples.title: Rehabilitation robot deployment
examples.text: The Bern Adaptive Rehabilitation Robot is used in daily treatment at twelve rehabilitation hospitals. A registered randomized trial involving 310 patients demonstrated improved task performance compared with dose-matched conventional treatment. ARTORG developed the control system and the operating protocol has been transferred to the participating hospitals.
examples.label_reason: Documented deployment and comparative evidence support substantial practical value.

examples.title: Conference poster attendance
examples.text: Three doctoral researchers presented posters at the regional engineering meeting. Their posters described work in progress and no new results were released. The group enjoyed networking with colleagues and thanked the conference organizers. Travel was supported by an internal student mobility allowance.
examples.label_reason: Meeting participation does not demonstrate a valuable finding.

examples.title: Standard workshop services
examples.text: The workshop offers standard milling and drilling for internal university projects. Users can request simple brackets and adapters through the usual ticket system. Prices cover materials and staff time. The announcement updates the opening hours and does not describe any distinctive equipment or novel technical capability.
examples.label_reason: Generic service with no evidence of distinctive or strategic capability.

examples.title: Completed surgical guidance breakthrough
examples.text: The Bern Optical Guidance project achieved the first fully image-guided procedure in the program's clinical series in 2001. Its navigation method was subsequently incorporated into three commercial surgical systems. ARTORG completed the project in 2005; the original research team is no longer operating this project.
examples.label_reason: Historical technical achievement with documented adoption; must not be labeled active.

examples.title: Interoperable insulin control validation
examples.text: The Open Insulin Control Validation program completed a randomized multicenter study with 420 adults. Its interoperable controller increased time in target range by 12 percentage points without increasing severe adverse events against the trial comparator. Diabetes Center Berne coordinated the study and released the validation protocol for independent replication.
examples.label_reason: Substantial comparative research result with concrete evidence and reusable protocol.

examples.title: Monthly newsletter subscription
examples.text: Subscribe to our monthly newsletter for updates from the diabetes technology community. Subscribers receive event invitations, staff interviews and links to recent publications. Enter your email address and confirm your subscription. This announcement contains no new study result, technology or research service.
examples.label_reason: Routine communications announcement.

examples.title: Independent glucose testing platform
examples.text: The Independent Glucose Testing Platform provides standardized dynamic glucose challenges, reference measurements and blinded device comparison. Its validated protocol has been adopted by eight manufacturers for independent performance evaluation. Diabetes Center Berne operates the platform and accepts external projects through its research services team.
examples.label_reason: Distinctive validated capability, documented adoption and access.

examples.title: Five publications announced
examples.text: Our researchers published five papers this month in several respected journals. The titles cover diabetes education, sensor preferences and general perspectives on digital health. The announcement provides neither findings nor methods and simply congratulates the authors. Readers are invited to consult the publication list.
examples.label_reason: Publication count alone does not establish significant findings.

examples.title: Home insulin stability technology
examples.text: The Home Insulin Stability technology measures loss of insulin activity using a validated optical cartridge. Independent testing in 600 samples showed 96 percent agreement with laboratory assays. Diabetes Center Berne supported development, and the patented cartridge was licensed for commercial manufacturing under a signed agreement.
examples.label_reason: Specific validated technology with documented commercialization.

examples.title: Exploratory questionnaire revision
examples.text: A small internal project revised the wording of a questionnaire for ten volunteers. Respondents found the revised instructions easier to read, but the project did not evaluate clinical outcomes or establish a validated instrument. The team plans to refine two questions before conducting a larger study.
examples.label_reason: Useful but secondary incremental work.

examples.title: National diabetes data infrastructure
examples.text: The National Diabetes Data Infrastructure links standardized longitudinal records from 22 clinical centers under a common research protocol. Diabetes Center Berne coordinates the CHF 18 million funded program. Approved researchers can access harmonized analyses through a documented application process, enabling studies that individual centers cannot support alone.
examples.label_reason: Strategic funded infrastructure and concrete research capability.

examples.title: Innovation funding applications open
examples.text: Applications are now open for the annual innovation funding competition. Selected teams may receive up to CHF 100,000 in support. No winners have been selected and no projects or results are announced. Applicants should submit a short proposal describing their idea and team before the deadline.
examples.label_reason: Funding opportunity, not an awarded program or achievement.

examples.title: Historic insulin delivery study
examples.text: The Bern Home Delivery Study established that automated dosing could be operated safely outside hospital in its controlled study of 180 participants. Its published operating protocol became the basis of a subsequent multicenter research program. Diabetes Center Berne completed the study in 2010, and recruitment is closed.
examples.label_reason: Significant historical result and subsequent adoption; completed status is explicit.

examples.title: Promotional product announcement
examples.text: A partner describes its new app as the world's best diabetes assistant. The announcement provides no evaluation data, regulatory status, deployment evidence or technical details beyond reminders and a dashboard. The company hopes the app will revolutionize care. Diabetes Center Berne shares the announcement as community news.
examples.label_reason: Unsupported promotional claims must not become validated capabilities.
